CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Best practice when working on Photography: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Photography.
   B. Damage equipment used for Photography.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Photography.
   D. Practise Photography with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

2. Best practice when working on Painting and Montage: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Painting and Montage.
   B. Practise Painting and Montage with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Damage equipment used for Painting and Montage.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Painting and Montage.

3. Best practice when working on Descant Recorder: (1 mark)

   D. Refuse all feedback on Descant Recorder.

9. Primary colours are: (1 mark)
   A. Green, orange, and purple
   B. Brown, pink, and gold
   C. Black, white, and grey
   D. Red, blue, and yellow

10. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.
   B. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.
   C. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. Warming up before sport helps to: (1 mark)
   A. Remove the need for rules
   B. Guarantee a trophy
   C. Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk
   D. Replace drinking water

12. Best practice when working on Indigenous Kenyan Games: (1 mark)

15. Best practice when working on Songs: (1 mark)

   B. Disrupt classmates during Songs.
   C. Practise Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Songs.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Rhythm and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Melody and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
